coordinate_system: Equatorial degrees; J2000/ICRS approximation supported by matched SIMBAD positions; atlas equinox not explicitly confirmed in supplied introduction
scope: 114 main chart numbers; no detail charts
status: Approximate reconstructed footprints; ten charts photo-fitted and all others extrapolated
method: Read projection type from supplied introduction.
Assume nominal chart center coordinates from overview-map reconstruction.
Rectify each physical leaf separately using its visible corners and nominal 26:28 page aspect ratio.
Manually identify graticule intersections or catalogued-object centres. New graticule controls were independently selected from enlarged image crops; ambiguous crossings were excluded.
Fit a similarity transform from spherical stereographic projection to rectified page coordinates.
Preserve the two overlapping leaves as separate boundary polygons.
For charts without photographs, use the median leaf geometry fitted to charts 4, 11, 21, 33, 45, 57, 107 and 113.
Fit charts 1 and 114 independently as single-page polar maps; south-polar RA0 points upward and north-polar RA0 points downward.

units.boundary_ra_dec_deg: Each vertex is [RA degrees, declination degrees].
units.projection_plane_corners_degree_equivale: Stereographic x,y in radians multiplied by 180/pi; x increases west/right, y increases north/up.
units.bbox_ra: Hours; endpoints unwrapped around chart centre, so values below zero or above 24 are intentional.

limitations: No publisher-certified geometry or accuracy tolerance.
Photo perspective, page curvature and manual point selection limit accuracy.
Calibration residuals are fit residuals, not independently measured boundary errors.
Directly sampled declinations are 0,+15,+30,+45,+60,+75,+90,-60,-75,-90. Bands -15,-30,-45 and other chart numbers are extrapolated from shared paper geometry.
South-polar page arrangement and orientation are confirmed by chart 114; individual unphotographed charts remain inferred.
Page polygons include printed coordinates and binding-hole areas; they do not subtract labels, holes or occluded artwork.
The sky appears on overlapping physical leaves. Do not concatenate their polygons as one simple polygon. Use a union or a logical OR for point inclusion.
Planar polygon algorithms must handle RA wrap; near poles, use inverse projection into each page rectangle or a spherical-polygon method.
Boundary polygons sample each edge at 50 intervals. Boxes use 200 samples per edge and are approximate; rounding does not imply that precision.
recommended_lookup: For each page, project a sky position using the stated stereographic centre, then test membership in its projection-plane quadrilateral. For polar charts use RA0=0 degrees. This avoids RA-wrap and spherical-edge approximation problems.
